newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr still bullish if retrace levels hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr still bullish if retrace levels hold.

text.p: The dollar, taking a pause after impressive gains, is likely to resume its climb unless it violates support at important retracement levels, analysts said on Tuesday.
Dollar/mark dipped to a low of 1.8272 after rocketing on Monday to 1.8490, its highest since November 1989.
But analysts pointed out dollar/mark may climb anew since it did not violate support at 1.8250, or the 38-percent retracement of the July 21/28 rally from 1.7860 to 1.8490.
They did not see a danger of reversal unless 1.5175, the 50-percent retracement of the same rally, is lost.
Near-term resistances are at 1.8410 and at the retest of the 1.8490 high, while 1.8610 remains the longer-term objective in a bull channel from November 1996.

"Dollar/mark had a bit of a pullback but is holding above 1.8250, the 38-percent retracement of the move to 1.8490," said Scott Siller, senior analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch who cautioned "trendline support may or may not be tested at 1.8175, a key point in the bull channel from July 10."
In early afternoon, the dollar was quoted at 1.8375/85 marks versus 1.8315/25 at the open, and at 118.22/32 yen vs. 117.60/65.
Analysts agreed the 1.8175-mark level would signal a trend reversal if it were to give way, since it is both a 50-percent retracement level and a key channel point.

Dollar/yen extended its gains above 118.00 to face little resistance on its way to 119.00, the 50-percent retracement of the move from the 1997 high of 126.47 to the low at 110.62. Strong support is at 117.00, the 38-percent retracement of the 1997 high/low move and a crucial point on a rising trendline from September 1995.
"Surely, 119.00 is big level, and then 120.00, the low from February 28 and March 3," Siller said.
Helping dollar/yen was the recovery of mark/yen above 64.00. The fall of 64.45, another important point in a six-day bull channel, would likely accelerate yen weakness.
Siller noted that taking out 64.50 would also violate a two-month bear trend and open the scope for a run to 66.00.
Another important retracement level was on dollar/Swiss where 1.5030, the 38-percent retracement of the July 18-28 rally from 1.4690 to 1.5250, provided solid support.
Also, the sterling correction seemed to have ran its course, with $1.6335 and 2.9725 marks the bottom, at least temporarily.
